text:
alertbot: ALERT: e2w p95 latency spike >140ms in gpu-pool-west-2b during peak batching (11:48-11:56). affected: gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-12. automatic triage attached.

maya: seeing the same in grafana — sudden p95/p99 jump aligned with batch window start. traces show tailbacks between nodes.

jason: i pulled dmesg + quick link stats on gpu-07. nothing obvious in dmesg, but link counters look odd.
```
ip -s link show dev eno2
2: eno2: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes  1234567890  packets  1234567  errors 0  dropped 0  overruns 0  frame 0
    TX: bytes  987654321  packets  987654  errors 0  dropped 0  carrier 0  collisions 0
```

priya: switch logs show lots of "ipfrag" events and some PMTUD-related notices around the windows. looks like fragmentation/DF interactions.

liam: ethtool -S on gpu-03 shows rx_missed_errors and rx_no_buffer rising during the spike:
```
ethtool -S eno1 | egrep "rx_missed|rx_no_buffer"
rx_missed_errors: 482
rx_no_buffer: 129
```

netwatch: quick hypothesis — MTU mismatch across the path + qdisc coalesce/GSO edge-case. some hosts in the pool got provisioned with mtu 9000, others with mtu 1500 after the recent bootimage change. when big segments get coalesced then hit a 1500 hop they get fragmented/dropped and we fall back to TCP layering -> latency.

maya: that matches the traces: RDMA paths looked clean but fallbacks to tcp/tls show the delays. rdma counters not showing remote error, so prob at L3/L2.

jason: i can push a quick mitigation: force mtu 9000 across nodes in the pool OR temporarily disable GSO/GRO on problem hosts. pros/cons?

priya: disabling GSO/GRO will increase CPU usage and per-token cost during peak. would need to size that.

liam: based on previous load tests disabling GSO resulted in ~+10-15% CPU on inference processes on these instance types. ballpark cost bump ~+$0.02-0.04/hr/node during sustained peak. cheaper to fix MTU mismatch if feasible.

ops-oncall: quick plan: 1) verify MTU on all hosts in gpu-pool-west-2b 2) roll MTU fix via ansible in small batches (drain 1 node at a time) 3) if we can't coordinate quickly, disable GRO/GSO on the three worst hosts as emergency stopgap.

netwatch: i pushed a small check into fleet-health to detect MTU != 9000 for gpu pools and created a patch that sets MTU to 9000 for affected hosts. applied to gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-12 already.

alertbot: ALERT: mitigations applied, re-evaluating.

maya: after MTU fixes p95 back down to ~15ms, p99 ~40ms. no packet loss in grafana. :white_check_mark:

jason: tcpdump snippet from gpu-07 before fix showed many fragments and DF drops:
```
11:50:12.123456 IP (frag 1/2) 10.1.3.7 > 10.1.3.12: frag (DF), id 0x1a2b
11:50:12.123459 IP 10.1.3.7 > 10.1.3.12: IPFrag failed, sending ICMP frag-needed
```

priya: follow-ups: audit provisioning image that flipped some hosts to 1500 MTU, add a preflight MTU check for pool joins, add qdisc/backlog alerts, and run a short cost analysis for the GRO/GSO fallback.

ops-oncall: filing post-incident ticket INFRA-842 with root cause (provisioning MTU drift) + mitigation checklist and cost estimates. assigning to eng-infra and net infra.

netwatch: added automated remediation to fleet-health; will monitor for 24h and then propose a permanent guardrail in the cluster autoscaler.

maya: incident cleared at 1998766099. thanks all. :thumbsup:
